useCase.name: Create the classes an academic session runs and set how each is structured

intent.name: class.create
intent.summary: Create a class for the open academic session, set whether it is Fixed or Subject Wise, and attach the subjects it carries. One step.

routesHere.text: nayi class add karo — Grade 9, subject wise, Physics Chemistry Biology ke saath
routesHere.gloss: add a new class — Grade 9, subject wise, with Physics Chemistry Biology

routesHere: set up a Fixed class called Prep with the standard subjects

routesHere.text: Grade 6 bana do, order 6, sab subjects ke saath
routesHere.gloss: create Grade 6, order 6, with all the subjects

request.text: Grade 4 mein section B bana do

routesElsewhere.note: A class is a structure and holds nobody; students are placed into sections (BR-10, UC-27-02 BR-1).

request.text: Grade 4 mein Chemistry add kar do

routesElsewhere.note: Attaching a subject to a class that exists is a change to it, not a creation.

request.text: naya subject bana do

routesElsewhere.note: Maintaining the subject list itself is out of scope here; a class attaches subjects that already exist.

request.text: agle session ki classes bana do

routesElsewhere.note: A class belongs to one academic session and is never carried between them by editing its session (BR-2). Next session's classes are created afresh, in a session the controller holds — see PR-5.

request.text: students ko is class mein daal do

routesElsewhere.note: Creating a class creates no sections and no students (BR-10).

steps.note: One step. The class is created for the academic session the controller holds — the session is never taken from the request (BR-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Name uniqueness, the subject requirement, the acting role and whether a session is open at all are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the class, its attached subjects and the audit entry together or not at all. It creates no sections and no students (BR-10) — it is a structure that other things key off. Once created, the class becomes readable by attendance, timetable, assignment and examination in the same request (BR-8).

operations.name: class.create
operations.idempotencyKey: class_name + session_id + branch_id, which is the same triple BR-3 uses to decide a class already exists
operations.purpose: Create a class for the open academic session with its type and the subjects it carries.

parameters.name: class_name
parameters.notes: 2 to 60 characters, unique within the academic session and branch (BR-3). Passed exactly as the school says it — Grade 4, Class IV, Prep are different names and the school's own is the one that appears on every register.

parameters.name: class_order
parameters.notes: Where the class sits in the school's sequence, so lists and promotion read in the right order. Only where the request states it; never inferred from the name, because Prep, Nursery and Grade 1 do not sort themselves.

parameters.name: class_type
parameters.notes: Fixed means every student takes the same subjects; Subject Wise means students take a selection, which changes how fees, timetables and results are calculated (BR-4). It cannot be changed once students are placed (BR-6), so it is never guessed.

parameters.name: subject_ids

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. A subject named here does not exist. Creating it is a separate act on the subject list.

parameters.notes: At least one is required — a class with no subjects cannot be timetabled, taught or examined (BR-5, E2).

parameters.name: compulsory_subject_ids
parameters.notes: Only meaningful for a Subject Wise class, where an optional subject is one a student may choose not to take. Omitted for a Fixed class, where every student takes everything.

parameters.name: age_range
parameters.notes: The ages the class normally takes, used to check an inquiry at the point it is submitted (UC-02-01 BR-3). Only where the request states it.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: subjects
fields.description: Those attached, with whether each is compulsory.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: The academic session it belongs to, and cannot leave (BR-2).

fields.name: published_to
fields.description: The modules that can now read it — attendance, timetable, assignment, examination (BR-8).

errors.meaning: A class of that name already exists in this session and branch.
errors.note: Message names the session. Two classes called Grade 4 in one session make every list ambiguous (BR-3).
Message: "Attach at least one subject. A class with no subjects cannot be timetabled, taught or examined."
A class belongs to a session, so there is nothing to create it in.

errors.meaning: A Coordinator attempted to create a class.
errors.note: Only a School Admin creates classes; Coordinators create the sections under them. In practice the capability is absent from a Coordinator's allow-list.

planningRules.rule: Never guess the class type. Fixed and Subject Wise change how fees, timetables and results are calculated (BR-4), and the type cannot be changed once a single student is placed (BR-6) — so a wrong guess is locked in for a whole session.
Never infer class_order from the name. Prep, Nursery, KG and Grade 1 do not sort themselves, and the order is what lists and promotion read.
Pass the class name exactly as the school says it. It appears on every register, invoice and result sheet, and the school's own wording — Grade 4, Class IV, Prep — is the one they will look for.

Never create a class to get past a refusal somewhere else. A section that cannot be created, an import row naming a class that does not exist, or a placement with nowhere to go are all statements about the structure — and creating the missing class silently invents part of the school's shape.
session_id and branch_id come from $session. A class for next year is created in next year's session, which the actor opens first; a plan never takes the session from the request (BR-2).
Never plan a class creation for a set. Each carries a type, an order and a subject list that someone decided; a batch decides none of them.

reversal.statement: There is no delete. A class no longer run is deactivated through class.deactivate, and even that is refused while it holds an active section or a placed student (BR-9). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

request.text: Grade 4 bana do, order 4, fixed class, sab standard subjects ke saath
request.gloss: create Grade 4, order 4, a fixed class, with all the standard subjects

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, academic session 2025-26.

steps.note: The type is Fixed because the request says so, not because Grade 4 usually is (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Grade 4 exists for 2025-26 and sections can be created under it (AC-1). No sections and no students exist yet — it is a structure (BR-10).

request.text: Grade 9 bana do — subject wise, Physics Chemistry Biology optional, baaqi compulsory
request.gloss: create Grade 9 — subject wise, Physics Chemistry Biology optional, the rest compulsory

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, academic session 2025-26.

inputs.subject_ids: $request.subjects_phrase → English, Urdu, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology

steps.note: compulsory_subject_ids is sent because the class is Subject Wise and the request distinguishes them. On a Fixed class it would be omitted entirely.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Grade 9 exists as Subject Wise with three compulsory subjects and three optional. That distinction now drives how its fees, timetables and results are calculated (BR-4).

request.text: Grade 4 bana do

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, where Grade 4 already exists for 2025-26.

steps.note: The plan is emitted unchanged; it does not check for the name beforehand. The API returns NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS (E1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is created. Report that Grade 4 already exists for 2025-26 — which usually means the actor wants a section under it, or is looking at the wrong session.

routesHere.gloss: set Grade 5's age range to 9 to 11

routesElsewhere.note: Capacity belongs to a section, not to a class.

request.gloss: change the class from fixed to subject wise

routesElsewhere.goesTo: class.update, and it may be refused
routesElsewhere.note: Permitted only while no student is placed in any of its sections (BR-6, E3). Once one is, the type is settled for the session.

request.text: is class ko agle session mein le jao
request.gloss: move this class to the next session

routesElsewhere.note: A class belongs to one academic session and is never carried between them by editing its session (BR-2). Next session's classes are created afresh.

steps.note: One step, carrying only what the request changes. Subjects are added and removed by explicit lists rather than by replacing the set, so a rename never quietly drops a subject.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The type change, subject removal and the acting role are enforced by the API and arrive as errors; the plan does not test for them beforehand.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself. The change is reflected everywhere the class is used, in the same request — a register printed after a name correction shows the corrected name (BR-8, AC-8). So a small edit here reaches attendance, timetable, assignment and examination immediately.

operations.name: class.update
operations.idempotencyKey: class_id + the changed field set and their new values
operations.purpose: Change a class's definition or the subjects it carries, and reflect the change everywhere the class is used.

parameters.name: class_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No active class of that name in this academic session and branch.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their class order and type.

parameters.notes: The class, resolved from how the actor named it — Grade 4, Class IV, the words the school uses. Scoped to the open academic session, because a class belongs to one and is never carried between them (BR-2).

parameters.name: class_name
parameters.notes: 2 to 60 characters, still unique within the session and branch (BR-3). Only where the request renames it.

parameters.name: class_order
parameters.notes: Only where the request states the new order.

parameters.name: class_type
parameters.notes: Only where the request changes it, and refused once students are placed in any of its sections (BR-6, E3). Never sent to 'correct' a type nobody questioned.

parameters.name: age_range
parameters.notes: Only where the request states it.

parameters.name: add_subject_ids
parameters.notes: Subjects to attach. A subject may be added mid-session (A3).

parameters.name: remove_subject_ids

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. That subject is not attached to this class.

parameters.notes: Subjects to detach. Refused where marks, a timetable slot or an assignment already exist against one in this session, because removing it would orphan work already done (BR-7, E4).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: subjects
fields.description: The subjects the class now carries.

fields.name: placed_student_count
fields.description: How many students are placed across its sections. Above zero, the type is settled for the session (BR-6).

fields.name: propagated
fields.description: The change is now visible on registers, timetables and result sheets (BR-8).

errors.meaning: The type was changed after students are placed.
errors.note: Message names the placed students. Changing the type would alter how their fees and results are calculated part way through a session (BR-6).

errors.meaning: A subject was removed that already carries marks, a timetable slot or an assignment.
errors.note: The message names the subject. Removing it would orphan work already done (BR-7).

errors.meaning: The new name is already used by another class in this session.
The removal would leave the class with no subjects.
errors.note: A class carries at least one subject (BR-5).

errors.meaning: The acting user is not a School Admin.

planningRules.rule: Send only what the request changes. Every field sent is a recorded change that propagates to attendance, timetable and examination in the same request (BR-8); resupplying an unchanged name records an edit nobody made and reprints registers for nothing.
Never send class_type unless the request changes it. It is refused once students are placed (E3), so including it in an unrelated edit turns a rename into a refusal and neither happens.

Add and remove subjects by explicit list, never by replacing the set. A replacement built from what the actor mentioned drops every subject they did not name, and E4 would only catch the ones already carrying work.

Never treat SUBJECT_IN_USE as an obstacle. Marks, a timetable slot or an assignment already exist against that subject this session, and removing it would orphan them — the answer is that the subject stays until the session ends.
Never rename a class to resolve a duplicate. E1 means two classes share a name in one session, and which one should change is the school's decision, not a tidy-up.
branch_id comes from $session, and the class is resolved within the open academic session. A class in a past session is not edited from this one (BR-2).

reversal.statement: There is no undo. A wrong change is changed again, and both stay in the audit log with their previous values. The propagation to registers, timetables and result sheets has already happened either way (BR-8). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

request.text: Grade 9 mein Chemistry add kar do, is saal chala rahe hain
request.gloss: add Chemistry to Grade 9, we are running it this year

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, academic session 2025-26.

steps.note: An explicit add. The existing subjects are not resupplied, so none of them can be dropped by accident (PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Chemistry is attached to Grade 9 mid-session (A3) and becomes available to its sections, its timetable and its examinations. Nothing else on the class changed.

request.text: Grade 7 se Art hata do, is saal nahi chal rahi
request.gloss: take Art off Grade 7, we are not running it this year

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, where Art already carries marks for this session.

steps.note: The plan is emitted unchanged; it does not check for marks beforehand. The API returns SUBJECT_IN_USE (E4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing changes. Report that Art already carries marks this session and cannot be removed — the work would be orphaned (BR-7). It can come off when next session's classes are created.

request.text: Grade 4 ko subject wise kar do

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, where 54 students are placed across Grade 4's sections.

steps.note: Emitted as asked. The API returns TYPE_CHANGE_REFUSED (E3) and names the placed students.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing changes. Report that 54 students are already placed, so the type is settled for this session — changing it would alter how their fees and results are calculated part way through (BR-6). Next session's Grade 4 can be created Subject Wise.

intent.name: class.deactivate
intent.summary: Deactivate a class the school no longer runs, once nothing is still attached to it. One step.
routesHere: deactivate Grade 11, we're not running it this year

routesHere.text: ye class ab nahi chal rahi, band kar do
routesHere.gloss: this class is no longer running, close it

routesHere: retire this class for the session

request.text: class delete kar do

routesElsewhere.note: A class is deactivated, never deleted (BR-9). Its history stays readable.

request.text: section band kar do

routesElsewhere.note: A class cannot be deactivated while an active section remains (BR-9, E5), so the sections go first.

request.text: students ko kahin aur shift kar do

routesElsewhere.note: Deactivation is refused while a placed student remains. Moving them is a separate act with its own reason.

steps.note: One step. Whether anything is still attached is the API's to enforce (BR-9, E5) — the plan does not count sections or students beforehand.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Active sections and placed students both refuse the deactivation, and the message names them.
plan.atomicity: One write: the class moves to Inactive with its audit entry, together or not at all. Nothing is deleted — the class, its subjects and everything recorded against it stay readable (BR-9). No section and no student is touched, because the deactivation is refused outright while either remains.

operations.name: class.deactivate
operations.idempotencyKey: class_id, since a class has one deactivation and a repeat changes nothing
operations.purpose: Mark a class inactive so it is no longer offered, keeping it and everything recorded against it readable.

parameters.name: class_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No active class of that name in this academic session and branch.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their class order and type.

parameters.notes: The class, resolved from how the actor named it — Grade 4, Class IV, the words the school uses. Scoped to the open academic session, because a class belongs to one and is never carried between them (BR-2).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The class as deactivated, or what is still holding it.

fields.name: active_section_count
fields.description: Zero on success. Above zero it is why the deactivation was refused.

errors.meaning: An active section or a placed student remains.
errors.note: The message names the counts — "2 active sections and 54 students" (AC-6). Each has to be dealt with as its own act; there is no cascade.

errors.meaning: The acting user is not a School Admin.

planningRules.rule: Never plan the clearing-up. STILL_IN_USE naming two sections and 54 students is the system saying a person has to decide where those children go (BR-9); moving them, or deactivating sections, are separate acts with their own reasons and their own consequences.
Never deactivate a class to correct a mistake in creating it. A class created in error still cannot be deleted, and a class deactivated in error is one the school can no longer use this session.
Report the counts when the deactivation is refused. They are the answer — the actor almost certainly did not know 54 students were still placed.

reversal.statement: The lifecycle holds Active and Inactive and no capability reactivates a class — the use case describes deactivation only. Where a class is deactivated in error, nothing here restores it. See OPEN-QUESTIONS.

request.text: Grade 11 band kar do, is saal nahi chala rahe
request.gloss: close Grade 11, we are not running it this year

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, where Grade 11 has no sections and no students.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Grade 11 is Inactive and no longer offered. Everything recorded against it stays readable (BR-9).

request.text: Grade 4 ko band kar do

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, where Grade 4 holds two active sections and 54 placed students.

steps.note: Emitted unchanged; the plan does not count anything beforehand. The API returns STILL_IN_USE (E5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing changes. Report that 2 active sections and 54 students are still attached, and that each has to be dealt with first — do not offer to move them (PR-1).

steps.note: In practice the capability is absent from a Coordinator's allow-list, so this plan is never built.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing changes. Report that only a School Admin may deactivate a class, and that Coordinators work at the section level.
